reviews.analysis: glibc glob expansion can consume CPU/memory with hostile patterns. The Go URL/HTML implementation does not call libc glob or expose filesystem wildcard input. Browser launch arguments and profile paths are operator-generated; no shell exists. Missing dynamic imports and these source checks are not a complete native call-graph proof, so accept residual risk rather than claiming absence. Confinement re-reviewed on 2026-10-20 for the blank-running-browser snapshot: customer contexts are created only after restore; every VM/browser is consumed once and terminated before payment/output. Removing the redundant run hook does not add reuse or reset admission. Native input, egress, sandbox and 15/20/45-second deadlines remain bounded. The 512 MiB baseline lowers the peak to 2 GiB; the worker now returns at most 4 MiB of uncompressed result JSON through bounded Go readers/serialization, without increasing native HTML input. The controller validates the full text/schema and constructs a complete ALB envelope, reserving the largest valid payment receipt, before settlement. Negotiated per-response gzip uses Go compress/gzip BestSpeed with a 765 KiB compressed-output bound; headers and payment receipts are never compressed into the source-data body. Unencodable output is rejected without settlement, additional truncation or bad-source attribution. No compression state is reused across requests. Stripping debug symbols preserves dynamic linking, exact library inventory and native regression checks. Local real-browser lifecycle/one-shot tests and private AWS rendering/clone-entropy checks passed. These changes do not patch this finding or prove its native path absent. Chromium 156.0.8078.47 upgrade reviewed against the same external-library versions and current Debian tracker entries, which still mark these reports unfixed. The archive is pinned to SHA256 955059fa7020d7be85eb503e21339fd4d718f51f5996d3b60633fbf908bda132. Chromium's version-tagged Expat build still lists Skia, libjingle_xmpp and Wayland consumers; this is not a complete call-graph proof. No native input, egress, sandbox or VM-lifecycle control is relaxed. The upgraded image must separately pass real-browser and private AWS regression checks before release. Launch hardening review: one additional VM launch is permitted only for the exact AWS terminal startup reason Internal service error., before authentication or any customer job is sent, after independently confirmed termination. Unknown states/reasons, cancellation, failed cleanup, transport, conversion and payment outcomes are never replayed by this change. Both launches share the original 35-second work deadline, use distinct identities and never overlap. Native input limits, single-use customer execution and teardown-before-payment remain unchanged; bounded infrastructure startup/read costs can increase for that failure. Regression tests cover the retry ceiling, unknown-reason refusal, no job/token before readiness and cleanup failure refusal. Deployment-policy review: allowing the inherited PaymentMode tag alongside Project fixes main-stack image creation without changing region/project requirements, runtime authority, native inputs, egress or VM lifecycle. Shared receiver logging preserves bounded panic/outcome diagnostics without recording panic values or source content; the credential-free browser worker has no server/telemetry dependency. No customer processing capability is added.
reviews.limitations: These libraries remain unpatched for this finding. Input restrictions, sandboxing and deadlines reduce impact; they do not prove unreachability or rule out other defects. No confidential upstream reproducer was available or used.
reviews.residualRisk: A hostile job may exhaust CPU/memory, crash or time out, and consume bounded paid-for infrastructure without collecting customer payment. Aggregate attacks across wallets remain possible. The 15-second browser deadline, 20-second worker budget, 45-second service-enforced VM lifetime and confirmed teardown constrain each attempt; they are not a zero-risk guarantee.
